questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only recognized food groups?
options: Protein, carbohydrate, lipids, water, minerals, vitamins, fibre
Protein, sugar, dairy, energy, water, minerals, fat
Carbohydrate, calcium, vitamins, glucose, fibre, protein
Lipids, meat, starch, water, minerals, vitamins, fibre

questions.question: Why might a pregnant woman require more of certain nutrients, such as iron, compared to a non-pregnant woman of the same age?
options: Because she needs to support the growth and development of the fetus
Because she is less active during pregnancy
Because iron is used to generate quick energy during daily exercise
Because her body stops absorbing other nutrients from food

questions.question: If 10 g of water rises in temperature by 5 °C when a piece of food is burned under it, how much energy (in Joules) was transferred to the water? (Use: Energy = mass of water × rise in temp × 4.2)
What is the main reason our body needs food as a source of building materials?
options: To make biomass for growth and to repair damaged tissues
To completely replace water lost through sweating
To produce carbon dioxide for our lungs
To prevent our muscles from moving

questions.question: Food provides fuel for cellular respiration. What is the primary purpose of cellular respiration in living organisms?
options: To generate oxygen for the atmosphere
To provide energy for essential life processes
To store unused water in the kidneys
To build protective outer shells on cells

questions.question: Where can you find information about the nutrient content and the daily recommended amounts of energy for a specific food product?
options: On the food packaging labels
In a dictionary of science terms
On the receipt from the supermarket
By weighing the food on a kitchen scale

questions.question: Which two units are commonly used on food packaging to compare the amount of energy provided by different foods?
options: Grams and kilograms
Kilojoules and calories
Milliliters and liters
Newtons and joules

questions.question: Which two measurements of a person are needed to calculate their Body Mass Index (BMI)?
options: Height and body mass
Waist circumference and age
Heart rate and lung capacity
Body mass and daily water intake

questions.question: What can happen to a person's BMI if they consistently consume much more food than their body needs?
options: Their BMI will decrease rapidly
Their BMI will remain completely unchanged
Their BMI will become too high, which can lead to obesity
Their BMI will fluctuate but always stay in the underweight range

questions.question: Obesity is a serious health condition. Which of the following is a long-term health issue that obesity increases the risk of developing?
options: Scurvy
Heart disease
Color blindness
Hemophilia

questions.question: What is the term for a disease caused specifically by a lack of a particular nutrient in a person's diet?
options: Infectious disease
Genetic disorder
Deficiency disease
Chronic disease

questions.question: What does the term "recovery time" mean in relation to exercise?
options: The time it takes for a person to run a fixed distance
The time it takes for the heart rate to return to its resting rate after exercise
The duration of the entire exercise session
The time spent sleeping after a heavy workout

questions.question: How does physical fitness generally affect a person's recovery time after exercise?
options: Fitter people have a shorter recovery time
Fitter people have a longer recovery time
Fitness has no effect on recovery time
Fitter people do not have a recovery time because their heart rate never increases

questions.question: In an investigation to see how different types of physical activities affect a student's pulse rate, what is the independent variable?
options: The pulse rate
The type or amount of exercise
The temperature of the room
The time of day the test is done

questions.question: If you are investigating the effect of exercise on heart rate, which of the following should be kept as a control variable to ensure a fair test?
options: The heart rate of the participant after exercise
The person performing the exercise and the duration of the exercise
The type of shoes worn by the observer
The total number of beats recorded during recovery

questions.question: When plotting a bar chart to compare the heart rates of students after three different types of exercises (walking, jogging, running), where should the type of exercise be placed?
options: On the y-axis, because it is continuous data
On the x-axis, because it is categoric data
In a key next to the graph only
On both the x-axis and the y-axis

questions.question: When plotting a bar chart of heart rate after different exercises, where should the dependent variable (heart rate) be placed?
options: On the y-axis
On the x-axis
Only in the title of the chart
Along a diagonal line across the chart

questions.question: Why do both breathing rate and heart rate increase when a person is exercising?
options: Because cells need more oxygen for cellular respiration to release energy
To prevent carbon dioxide from entering the body
Because the body needs to cool down by taking in cold air
To allow the muscles to store more undigested food

questions.question: When investigating the energy in food by burning it under a test tube of water, what is directly measured to determine how much energy was released?
options: The volume of smoke produced
The change in temperature of the water
The change in the mass of the water
The brightness of the flame

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding human health?
options: People have only physical health, while mental health is not a recognized concept
People have both physical health and mental health
Mental health is only important for adults, not school-aged children
Physical health and mental health are completely unrelated to lifestyle
